script: High school nose bleeds forced me home—what my teachers never told me.. I was in senior year, high blood pressure on a daily cycle, nose bleeding like a faucet that never stops. The school had to send me home more times than I could count because the law said if I was bleeding for a while, my parents had to pick me up. Most teachers were chill—just get up, go to the nurse, no permission needed. But Ms. Thompson? She was the queen of "no interruptions" and she'd yell at anyone who didn't have her say. So there I was, notebook open, mind on the lecture, when my nose starts a full‑blown bleed. I pinch, I angle my head back, but the blood just floods my notes and starts dripping onto the desk. I raise my hand, calm as a cucumber, "Can I be excused to the nurse?" She keeps talking for five minutes, pretending not to see me. Finally she points at me, "I'll answer your question after I finish." I am a petty person who's used to bleeding, so I decide, "Fine, I'll just sit and bleed here." I flip my hands to keep the mess off the floor—my elbows soaked, my forearms a watercolor of red. When she finally wraps up, she calls my name, "Did my lecture answer your question?" I stand, both hands and forearms drenched, "Can I go to the nurse?" She turns white, screams, "Why did you wait so long?! Go now!" She sends a friend to make sure I don't collapse in the hallway, but honestly I am more worried about a blood puddle on the carpet than a faint. Shortly after, the school updates policy: no permission needed to go to the nurse if you're bleeding. The audacity, right? I learned two things: one, teachers can be the worst, and two, my own body was my best ally.
